title: A car: accelerate, cruise, brake with ABS
subject: mechanics
statement: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at {a1} m/s^2 for {t1} s. It then travels at constant speed for {t2} s, and then brakes with ABS, slowing uniformly at {a3} m/s^2 until it stops. (a) Find its top speed. (b) How far does it go while accelerating? (c) How long and how far does it take to stop? (d) Find the total distance and the average speed. (e) The tyres' coefficient of friction on the road is {mu}: what is the greatest deceleration without skidding?

parts.hint: The car speeds up for t1 seconds from rest: which equation links u, a, t and v?

steps.say: Start from rest, so u is zero. The speed after the first phase is u plus a one times t one.

parts.hint: On a v-t graph, distance is an area.

steps.goal: Use s = u t + a t^2 / 2
steps.say: The distance is half a one t one squared, the area of the triangle under the speed graph.

parts.ask: the time and distance to stop
parts.hint: It slows from v1 to zero at a3.

steps.say: The time to stop is v one divided by a three.
The braking distance is v one squared over two a three.

parts.ask: the total distance and the average speed
parts.hint: Add the three distances; average speed is distance over time.

steps.say: At constant speed the distance is v one times t two.
Average speed is total distance over total time.

parts.hint: Friction can be at most mu times the normal force.

steps.say: The most friction can give is mu m g, so the deceleration is at most mu g, whatever the mass.

summary: Split the motion into phases with constant acceleration
Distance is the area under the v-t graph
ABS keeps the tyres rolling, so static friction (up to mu g) slows the car
